annotation.kind: faithfulness rebuild of the ordinary SylR execution, first-order recurrence, equation (20), and logarithmic-stability conclusion

assumptions: The exact top problem is A*R-R*B=-C in real arithmetic and has positive Frobenius separation.
The dimension is the positive power of two n=2^depth, and A and B have the upper-triangular block structure used by SylR.
The proof-carrying execution records SylR's four recursive solves in the order R21, R11, R22, R12 and the exact right-hand sides (15)-(18).
Equation (19), the page-86 first-order product and right-hand-side error estimates, and the scalar base-case rounding bound hold for the recorded execution family.
The multiplication-error factor mu is nonnegative, monotone, at least one at positive dimensions, and polynomially bounded.
The model is the finite real-valued first-order regime; exceptional values and the higher-order terms suppressed by the source derivation are outside the claim.

conditions.L: The identical fixed statement and P10 shared files are present; the frozen NumStability library is also present.
conditions.N: The fixed statement and P10 shared files are present; no NumStability artifact is present.

formal_statement.lean_header: theorem p10_t3_sylr_logarithmic_stability {depth : Nat} (run : P10SylRRun depth) : P10SylRLogarithmicallyStable run
formal_statement.plain_language: For a proof-carrying first-order execution of the paper's power-of-two SylR algorithm, derive the four-block error recurrence, the explicit equation-(20) forward bound, its comparison with a conventional solver, and the logarithmic condition-number exponent.

informal_proof: Choose a node attaining the worst first-order error at each level. Sum its four algorithm-linked block estimates to derive the source recurrence with coefficients 4, 2, 3, and mu(n/2). The variational separation certificate gives (norm(A)+norm(B))/sep at least one, while A*R-R*B=-C gives norm(C) at most (norm(A)+norm(B))*norm(R). Unroll the affine recurrence, bound its geometric sum, identify 6^depth with n^(1+log_2(3)), and rewrite the result relative to the conventional forward-error scale.
informal_statement: The ordinary SylR algorithm satisfies the first-order recurrence on printed page 86, the equation-(20) bound, and the paper's logarithmic-stability comparison.
paper_version: published journal version; volume 108, 2007, printed pages 59-91
